purpose: Define the correctness contract for Wisp's Monokl adapter, derived code-evidence publication, incremental refresh, and optional Git-history ranking signals.
scope: Covers typed projection of Monokl code facts into Wisp, derived code-evidence and impact records, complete publication semantics, incremental reconciliation, briefing selection provenance, and evaluation gates for weak history-derived signals.
non_goals: Implementing syntax parsers, semantic resolvers, or language-server lifecycle in Wisp
Persisting copied Monokl ASTs or building a second authoritative code index
Treating co-change or ownership as dependency or impact proof
Requiring generation machinery for an update that fits in one atomic transaction
Changing WISP-001 or WISP-002 artifact-validation scope

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every code-backed Wisp record carries the producing operation, analyzer/backend name and version, configuration digest, input content digest, workspace fingerprint, scope completeness, and capability precision supplied by Monokl.
Resolved, ambiguous, unresolved, and external outcomes remain distinct across the CLI adapter, library adapter, derived store, briefing compiler, and structured output boundaries.
An ambiguous outcome retains every candidate identity and its diagnostic in the typed result; ranking or budget truncation never changes its status to resolved.
When Monokl is unavailable, unsupported, timed out, or degraded, Wisp returns an artifact-only briefing with a typed gap and does not synthesize missing code facts.
A derived-state refresh that fits in one SQLite transaction publishes all replacement rows atomically, and a failed transaction leaves the previous complete state readable.
If a refresh spans multiple transactions or coordinated caches, readers select only the monotonically recorded last complete generation; they never observe staged rows from an incomplete generation.

For generated no-op, modify, edit-revert, create, delete, rename, configuration-change, and analyzer-version-change sequences, canonical derived state after each incremental step equals a clean rebuild from the resulting canonical inputs.
Filesystem watcher events are treated as invalidation hints and every refresh reconciles current files and content digests before publication.
Each Git-history signal records a stable signal kind, repository/window basis, source revision, and selection contribution, and is never represented as a Monokl dependency edge.

A history-derived signal remains disabled by default until a frozen Prism ablation reports intrinsic relevance, task outcome, false positives, latency, and context cost against an otherwise identical baseline.
